caseStudy.title: Portugal Fashion Experience 2025 — Backstage
body: Backstage documentation created during Portugal Fashion Experience 2025, photographed inside a fast-moving environment with constantly changing light, people and situations.
Rather than approaching the event as straightforward documentation, I focused on the atmosphere surrounding the show — transitions between spaces, details, preparation and spontaneous moments.
The visual language was developed around the energy and unpredictability of backstage, followed by selection, colour treatment and final post-production after the event.

caseStudy.title: BTS — LOSIENTO × David Bruno
body: Behind-the-scenes content created around the collaboration between LOSIENTO and David Bruno.
The approach was intentionally informal and observational, staying close to the people, spaces and moments surrounding the production rather than making the process feel overly staged.
Photography and VHS-style video were used together to create a more immediate and imperfect record of the collaboration, followed by editing and post-production for digital communication.

caseStudy.title: LOSIENTO × Watered Marta
body: A fashion-focused still and moving-image series created around the LOSIENTO × Watered Marta collaboration.
Photography and short-form video are treated as one visual language, using portraiture, styling, movement and close attention to the garments to keep the campaign coherent across formats.
The final selection brings the stills and videos together as a connected set of assets for digital communication, with a consistent treatment across capture and post-production.

caseStudy.title: Unmade Collection — LOSIENTO
body: A series of fashion films created for LOSIENTO around the Unmade Collection.

The visual approach was developed in dialogue with the identity of the collection, using movement, framing, texture and editing to translate the clothing into moving images rather than treating the videos simply as product documentation.
I worked across the concept, filming and post-production, adapting the rhythm, effects and transitions of each piece while maintaining a coherent visual language across the campaign.

caseStudy.title: Merch Drop — Traz os Monstros
body: For the launch of a new Traz os Monstros merchandise drop, I developed a visual approach designed to present the pieces without disconnecting them from the identity of the project.
The images balance product clarity with an editorial language, treating composition, light, framing and atmosphere as part of the same visual system.
The session was built to work across different contexts — from more descriptive catalogue images to photographs with a stronger visual presence for social media and the communication of the drop.
I was responsible for the visual concept, photography and final image treatment, keeping consistency across the different pieces.

caseStudy.title: Album / Artwork — Traz os Monstros
body: A collection of album-related visual material developed around the broader identity of Traz os Monstros.
Photography, graphic treatment and object-based imagery are brought together to create a rough, tactile visual language that can extend beyond a single cover or format.
The pieces are treated as parts of the same visual world, keeping the album artwork and supporting images connected rather than isolated.

caseStudy.title: Visuals — Traz os Monstros
body: An experimental set of visual pieces developed for Traz os Monstros across still and moving image.
The work uses distortion, repetition, collage-like image treatment and motion to expand the project’s identity beyond conventional promotional content.
This section works as a visual testing ground, connecting graphic experimentation with short-form video and digital communication.

caseStudy.title: BTS / Process — Traz os Monstros
body: A more observational record of the process around Traz os Monstros, focused on the moments that sit between finished releases and staged imagery.
The photography and video keep a direct, informal quality, using the working process itself as part of the visual identity rather than hiding it behind the final result.

caseStudy.title: Video Series — Traz os Monstros
body: A series of short-form videos created around Traz os Monstros for digital communication.
The work is driven by rhythm, performance and fast visual ideas, with editing used to keep each piece distinct while still belonging to the same broader visual world.

caseStudy.title: SEIS
body: Product photography developed for SEIS, with a visual approach built around presenting the pieces clearly while maintaining a strong and controlled image.
Composition, lighting, background and framing were considered as part of the same visual system, allowing the product itself to remain the central element.
I was responsible for the concept, photography and final retouching, producing a consistent set of images for the brand’s commercial communication.

caseStudy.title: Not Found
body: A collaborative visual project developed with NotFound.
The concept was built jointly, combining both perspectives into a shared visual language rather than following a predefined commercial brief.
I worked on the development of the visual approach, captured the material and handled the final editing, shaping the collaboration into a coherent final series.

caseStudy.title: Portrait Studies
body: Portraits made across different settings, from close views of a face to wider frames that retain part of the surrounding space. The selection brings together direct gazes, profiles and moments where the subject turns away from the camera.

Colour and monochrome are used across the series. Blue backgrounds, warm light and waterside settings give the photographs different visual treatments, while framing keeps the person central to each image.
I photographed and edited the series, shaping the final selection through crop, colour and contrast.

caseStudy.title: Monochrome Portraits
body: A portrait series built around a single subject and a consistent monochrome treatment. Side light catches the face, hands and hair while the background stays dark.
Changes in crop, gaze and gesture give each photograph a different emphasis. The sequence moves between wider portraits and close views, keeping strong shadow areas as part of the composition.
I developed the series and handled photography and image editing, working on contrast and tonal separation across the final selection.

caseStudy.title: Altered Images
body: Photographic images reworked through tonal inversion and changes in colour and contrast. Faces, clothing and urban backgrounds become elements that can be obscured, isolated or brought into conflict.

Some images keep a recognisable portrait; others shift attention towards silhouette, texture and colour. The editing changes how the photographed scene is read while retaining traces of the original setting.
I created the photographs and developed the experimental treatment, taking each image from capture through its final edit.

caseStudy.title: Natural Forms
body: Photographs of vegetation, water and small details, with attention to how light separates a subject from its surroundings. Bright stems against dark backgrounds, dense foliage and the surface of the sea set the visual range of the series.

The framing moves between recognisable scenes and tighter views where texture and colour carry the image. Green, blue and violet tones connect the photographs while leaving room for the differences between each setting.
I photographed and edited the series, choosing the framing, colour and contrast for each image.

caseStudy.title: SoaresBlend
body: A series of promotional videos developed for SoaresBlend, created to translate the brand into short-form visual content.
Each piece was built around its own concept and narrative structure, with attention to framing, movement, pacing and colour treatment throughout the production and post-production process.
I was responsible for the concept, filming and editing, shaping each video around the needs of the brand while keeping a consistent visual language across the series.
